chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:

Abū Baṣīr asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) while I was present, and he said: “May I be your ransom, how many times was the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) taken on the Ascension?” He said: “Twice. Jibrāʾīl made him stop at a station and said to him: ‘Stay in your place, O Muḥammad, for you have stood at a station at which no angel has ever stood, nor any prophet. Surely your Lord performs salat.’ He said: ‘O Jibrāʾīl, and how does He perform salat?’ He said: ‘He says: Subbūḥun, Quddūs, I am the Lord of the angels and the Spirit; My mercy has preceded My wrath.’ So he said: ‘O Allah, Your pardon, Your pardon.’”
He said: “And it was as Allah said: ‘two bow-lengths or nearer.’”

Then Abū Baṣīr said to him: “May I be your ransom, what is ‘two bow-lengths or nearer’?” He said: “What is between its curve and its tip.” He said: “Between them was a veil, glittering and trembling, and I only know it as that he said: of zabarjad. Then he looked through something like the eye of a needle toward whatever Allah willed of the Light of Majesty.”

Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “O Muḥammad.” He said: “At Your service, my Lord.” He said: “Who is for your community after you?” He said: “Allah knows best.” He said: “ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Amīr al-Muʾminīn, the master of the Muslims, and the leader of the radiant ones.” He said: Then Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said to Abū Baṣīr: “O Abā Muḥammad, by Allah, the wilayah of ʿAlī (عليه السلام) did not come from the earth; rather, it came from heaven directly.”

key_terms.سُبُّوحٌ قُدُّوسٌ: an expression of absolute glorification and holiness
key_terms.عُرِجَ: was taken up in the Ascension
key_terms.قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنَى: the measure of two bow-lengths or nearer, indicating utmost nearness
key_terms.وَلَايَةُ عَلِيٍّ: the divinely ordained authority of ʿAlī (عليه السلام)
key_terms.يُصَلِّي: performs salat; here describing a divine act as stated in the narration

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the Prophet’s Miʿrāj and the heavenly designation of Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts part of the Miʿrāj of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), describing his nearness, the divine proclamation of mercy, and a veiled vision of the Light of Majesty. It also presents the designation of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام) as the divinely appointed authority after the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله), affirming that his wilayah came from heaven.
